message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The genes that control mane growth are expressed dominantly, so even if a male lion inherits only one copy of the mane allele from one parent, he will develop a full mane. Other dominant traits include the typical tawny coat color (black pigment alleles are recessive).
